recipes.name: No-Fail Bean Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.1 ounce) package double-crust pie pastry, thawed
2 (15.5 ounce) cans navy beans, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Place each pie pastry into a 9-inch pie pan.

Place navy beans and evaporated milk into a food processor. Add sugar, melted butter, eggs, egg yolks, flour, vanilla, cinnamon, and nutmeg; pulse a few times, then process until smooth, about 1 minute. Pour mixture into the prepared pie crusts.
Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes, then reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and bake until filling is set and crust is golden brown, about 35 more minutes.
Remove from the oven and let cool for 1 hour before slicing.

raw_recipe.headline: No-Fail Bean Pie
raw_recipe.description: This bean pie is a traditional Muslim recipe made with canned navy beans, evaporated milk, and sugar. It's similar to pumpkin pie but not as sweet.

review.reviewBody: Great taste. I used soy milk instead of the evaporated milk, and changed the 2 1/2 cups sugar to 2 cups sugar and 1/4 cup pear butter, because I thought that the sugar amount was more than I wanted to deal with! The amount of filling was enough for 2 pies rather than one with a top crust! I baked the pies at 350 for 1 hr. 10 mins.

My husband loves bean my, but I didn't know how to make it...until now! He loved the pie. We had a place in our neighborhood but they closed. I followed some user tips and my own tweaks 2 1/4 cup white sugar and 1 tblsp brown sugar, baked at 350 for 1h 10m. The pies turned out great after they settled. I used a blender to mix the ingredients DONT OVER PULSE. The batter will be a bit loose but will bake up great. The next day they are even better, the color deepens and the flavor is awesome. Who knew you could turn beans into a delicious dessert, gonna add a little whip topping and next time use the egg whites as a little merguie.

To call this a traditional Muslim dish, it might be best to specify the vanilla extract must be alcohol free. That said, I made this as directed and with the frozen pie crusts in the foil pans. I think the bean mixture could have used twice as much time in the food processor (I kept getting bits of bean skin that was texturally distracting) and they got rather dark after the first 15 minutes at 450. I would suggest that you bake in the bottom third of the oven or use a pie shield/foil wrap the crust. The pie has a nice flavor and a very curious texture.

I followed the recipe to my personal taste. I like pretty much all my pies sweet except pies with meat or without berries. When I made this I followed the recipe I found but added more vanilla, sugar, butter, and even added brown sugar to the recipe. What I got was so scrumptious before I put it in the oven...I was so excited. Now I have the pie setting and cooling off. I made this pie from scratch. The crust was from flour, brown sugar, and butter. Wow! This crust is so good! I'm excited about this pie. Oh and I soaked the beans over night. Then I got a huge cheesecloth and cover the inside pot with the cloth. I then put the beans in the middle and folded the cheesecloth. I poured water around the inside of the pot and boiled the beans for a few hours. I smashed the beans a few times. Having the cheesecloth prevented the beans from burning and it kept the beans moist. I would recommend using cheesecloth.

This is the right pie. I do agree the crust is usually home made because of the lard (pork) in store bought crust. I would say that there were a lot of different recipes used or at least several because I remember my mother trying different ones to figure out the best one. I was a taste tester some 40/45 years ago. The only thing I would change is that I thought there was some brown sugar used or that a few versions had brown sugar. Versions would vary by state. I live in Ky and it was whiter looking pie like the one picture in Ohio. Chicago had another version, Milwaukee another. I made this one with half the sugar being white sugar and half brown and I thought it was accurate in taste. Thanks for submitting this

This was my first time attempting to make a bean pie, and it went very well! I made a few adjustments to the recipe as written. I used 1 cup of white sugar and 1.5 cups of dark brown. I only used a half teaspoon of nutmeg. I used 3 teaspoons of vanilla rather than 2. I used 3 eggs and 2 yolks rather than 2 eggs and 2 yolks.I used a blender rather than a food processor. I baked on 350 the entire time rather than switching temps. The recipe makes 2 pies.

This recipe was easy to follow and tastes great! Like most commenters, I reduced the sugar to 2 cups. For those who are lactose sensitive, I used lactose free half and half instead of evaporated milk. This is a keeper! To get that nice brown top, keep it in the preheated 450 degrees oven the full 15 minutes and then reduce to 350. The light bottom is due to blending those navy beans with the milk until very smooth.

My very first time making this recipe and very first time tasting a bean pie!! I followed this recipe almost to a T. I only used 1 3/4 cups of sugar, I used dried great northern beans (let them soak all day), I used a premade graham cracker crust, and I used my vitamix. It was so creamy and sweet and delicious!! Would never be able to tell I used beans, because it does not taste like beans at all. I love the cinnamony taste!! Excellent recipe!!

I love this recipe and always revisit it. I swap out evaporated for unsweetened canned coconut milk and white sugar for coconut sugar because of food allergies but it’s been in our lives for over a decade now. Thank you so much!

I made it just as the recipe said. In doing so I got three pies. I used Pillsbury pre made pie crust (14 oz 2 shells). Next time I will reduce the sugar to 1 & 3/4 cup for less grams of sugar. This a edit because I just made it again and only got the 2 pies. Must have done something wrong on my first try 🤔

I altered it a bit, I used 1 1/2 cup of granulated sugar with 1/2 cup of brown sugar, I used 4 eggs and baked both pies at 350 degrees for 1 hour (I also had extra filling left. This recipe is absolutely amazing and I've never had bean pie before.
Absolutely AMAZED!!!!! Never considered a pie to be a protein source. I will definitely be adding to my usual culprit list!!!

This pie is tasty and easy to make. I’ve made this using the suggested bean and using other white beans. All tasty!! Try it for yourself!!

As a born and raised Muslim I can say this is a pretty good recipe! I used northern beans as they were out of navy beans and it taste great ! I also didn’t have flour never used flour before but all in all it’s a great recipe !
